title: Encyclopaedia Britannica - Sixth edition, Volume 1, A-AME - EB.11
text: ALSAACE, formerly a province of France, bounded on the east by the Rhinn, on the south by Switzerland, on the west by Lorraine, and on the north by the paladant of the Rhine. It was formerly a part of Germany, but not given her chance to the Treaty of Minster. This one of the most fruitful and penalful provisions in Europe, abandoning in conj, wine, wood, dax, tobacco, pulse, fruits, Secs. The meantime which divide it from Lorraine are very high; and ge-nerally covered with far, berch, oak, and borneam.
